correctness.rationale: In a block of size b, the Pawlak boundary contains the whole block if the sample is nonempty and proper, and none otherwise. The two excluded events have total probability q_b, and disjoint blocks have independent contributions. Singleton factors are 1. For b>=2 the odds ρ_b=(1−q_b)/q_b are known and positive; normalize by the positive constant term F(0). The coefficient in degree b after cancelling only known factors in degrees below b is exactly m_bρ_b: multiple selections of a degree-b factor and all higher factors have degree >b. Apply this in the truncated power-series ring through degree K or through deg F for the full inversion; an empty universe and an all-singleton partition both correctly give F=1. Knowing |X| recovers the singleton number by subtraction. The sharp raw-prefix example at p=1/2 gives equal constants 2^(−2K−2), no positive terms through K, fixed total 2K+4 and two classes, yet only (K+1,K+3) has positive coefficient in degree K+1. The rough-pair lattice is the independent block product of two- and three-element chains. At p=1/2 the profiles (2,4) and (3,3) both have two three-element factors but clearly different boundary laws. In a fresh integer replay (`python3 /workspace/review-evidence/exact_checks.py`), all 291 partition/bias cases and 71865 subset evaluations agreed with factorization. This does not prove general inversion. The frozen verify_boundary.py was inspected, not run; its use of int.bit_count() requires Python 3.10+, not the stated 3.8 minimum.

value.rationale: The boundary is a canonical rough-set observable. Its size law distinguishes equivalence granulations of fixed universe size even when their abstract rough-set lattices are indistinguishable, and the sharp degree cutoff specifies precisely which sizes survive a restricted exact observation. This is an interpretable inverse classification and a concrete information-loss witness, not just a routine calculation of a PGF or expectation.
